tool: EasyMultiProfiler (EMP) — R multi-omics workflow for microbiome research
strengths: Unified five-module pipeline (extraction→visualization) on SummarizedExperiment/MultiAssayExperiment; standardised, reproducible microbiome multi-omics integration.
limitations: Restricted to microbiome/host-microbiome contexts; advanced modules assume R/Bioconductor proficiency; community validation still maturing.

tool: MOFA — statistical framework for unsupervised multi-omics integration
strengths: Discovers shared and modality-specific latent factors; handles missing values and heterogeneous variance; yields interpretable factor loadings.
limitations: Linear-Gaussian core limits non-linear modelling; scaling to very large or single-cell datasets requires MOFA+ extensions.

tool: mixOmics — R/Bioconductor package for multi-omics integration
strengths: Mature PLS-based integrative methods (sPLS, DIABLO) with built-in feature selection and rich visualisation across multiple omics.
limitations: Predominantly linear methods; native scalability limited for very large single-cell datasets; some methods require careful tuning.

tool: MOFA+ — scalable framework for single-cell multi-modal omics
strengths: Variational-inference extension of MOFA; flexible sparsity priors; joint decomposition across multiple sample groups and modalities.
limitations: Steep learning curve; designed primarily for single-cell multi-modal data; downstream interpretation often needs ML expertise.

tool: Similarity Network Fusion (SNF) — multi-omics integration method
strengths: Builds and fuses per-modality sample similarity networks into a unified graph; effective for subtype discovery across heterogeneous data.
limitations: Sensitive to similarity-network hyperparameters; lacks native missing-data handling; limited interpretability of the fused network.

tool: phyloseq — R/Bioconductor package for microbiome census analysis
strengths: Object-oriented infrastructure for reproducible import, manipulation, statistical analysis and graphics of 16S/metagenomic data.
limitations: Single-omics (microbiome-only) with no native multi-omics integration; newer specialised algorithms live in sibling packages.

tool: MetaboAnalyst 6.0 — web platform for metabolomics analysis
strengths: Unified web platform for LC-MS metabolomics processing, statistics, MS2 annotation and interpretation across ~130 species.
limitations: Focused on metabolomics; web deployment limits data size; native multi-omics integration remains comparatively limited.

tool: QIIME 2 — extensible microbiome data analysis platform
strengths: Standardised, reproducible, extensible microbiome workflows with plugin architecture and shareable analysis artifacts.
limitations: Microbiome-only, not a native multi-omics framework; plugin compatibility and learning curve can hinder new users.

tool: MicrobiomeAnalyst — web tool for microbiome statistical, visual and meta-analysis
strengths: Comprehensive web-based statistical, visual and meta-analysis for 16S and shotgun metagenomic/metatranscriptomic datasets.
limitations: Single-omics focus; web upload constraints on dataset size; multi-omics integration largely outside its core scope.

tool: MUUMI — R package for multi-omics meta-analysis and network integration
strengths: Unifies statistical meta-analysis with network-based integration (SNF, interactome inference) to identify robust molecular signatures.
limitations: Newer R package with narrower adoption; performance depends on availability and quality of underlying interactome priors.

tool: BioNeuralNet — Python graph-neural-network framework for multi-omics networks
strengths: Modular Python framework using GNNs for end-to-end multi-omics network construction, embedding and downstream analyses.
limitations: Requires familiarity with graph neural networks and Python ML ecosystems; computational cost scales steeply with network size.

tool: Profiler — open-source Python/Streamlit web platform for multi-omics analysis
strengths: Modular web platform with QC, statistics, ML/deep-learning, biomarker discovery, enrichment and survival analysis across modalities.
limitations: Currently emphasises proteomics, transcriptomics, lipidomics and EEG; web deployment constraints; still building community adoption.
